flags: No road construction narrative or authoritative designation date is cached. The history paragraph covers river protection and monument creation without equating either with byway designation.

NM 378 ends at the BLM boundary in the highway source; the recreation-area article treats a 13-mile byway as NM 378. The story distinguishes the numbered highway from the continuing paved road and omits total mileage.

Cerro and the visitor center have limited story evidence; their moments remain brief. La Junta concentrates on the confluence and its tributary rather than adding unrelated geology. The temperature record was dropped as unrelated, not unsupported.

Material strip miles run from La Junta toward Cerro. This narrative takes the reverse approach from NM 522, placing Cerro, visitor center and La Junta in that order; no coordinates were invented for the latter two.

BLM cache reports no water available, including campgrounds, and daylight road construction. Construction is included as an essential driving note; water availability and inconsistent fee information require review before any visitor-service fields are published.
